# Lab 10.15: Isolate a 3-tier Application

## What We Are Going to Do
Use service-account-based firewall rules so the web tier talks only to the app tier, and the app tier only to the database tier.

## Steps

1. **Create a network and one service account per tier.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud compute networks create tier-vpc --subnet-mode=custom
gcloud compute networks subnets create tier-subnet --network=tier-vpc --region=us-central1 --range=10.30.0.0/24

for t in web app db; do gcloud iam service-accounts create $t-sa; done</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **Create the firewall rules by service account.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SA=iam.gserviceaccount.com
gcloud compute firewall-rules create web-from-internet --network=tier-vpc \
  --allow=tcp:80 --source-ranges=0.0.0.0/0 --target-service-accounts=web-sa@$PROJECT_ID.$SA

gcloud compute firewall-rules create app-from-web --network=tier-vpc \
  --allow=tcp:8080 --source-service-accounts=web-sa@$PROJECT_ID.$SA \
  --target-service-accounts=app-sa@$PROJECT_ID.$SA

gcloud compute firewall-rules create db-from-app --network=tier-vpc \
  --allow=tcp:5432 --source-service-accounts=app-sa@$PROJECT_ID.$SA \
  --target-service-accounts=db-sa@$PROJECT_ID.$SA

gcloud compute firewall-rules create ssh-from-iap --network=tier-vpc \
  --allow=tcp:22 --source-ranges=35.235.240.0/20</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **Create one small VM per tier.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">for t in web app db; do
  gcloud compute instances create $t-vm --zone=us-central1-a --machine-type=e2-micro \
    --subnet=tier-subnet --no-address --service-account=$t-sa@$PROJECT_ID.$SA --scopes=cloud-platform \
    --metadata=startup-script='apt-get install -y netcat-openbsd; nc -lk -p 8080 &amp; nc -lk -p 5432 &amp;'
done</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


4. **Test the paths.** SSH to `web-vm` through IAP and test the app and database ports:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud compute ssh web-vm --zone=us-central1-a --tunnel-through-iap \
  --command="nc -zv -w3 APP_VM_IP 8080; nc -zv -w3 DB_VM_IP 5432"</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Web to app on 8080 succeeds. Web to database on 5432 times out.

5. **Use Connectivity Tests.** Go to **Network Intelligence → Connectivity Tests** and create a test from `web-vm` to `db-vm` on TCP 5432. It shows which rule blocks the traffic.

6. **Clean up.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud compute instances delete web-vm app-vm db-vm --zone=us-central1-a --quiet
gcloud compute firewall-rules delete web-from-internet app-from-web db-from-app ssh-from-iap --quiet
gcloud compute networks subnets delete tier-subnet --region=us-central1 --quiet
gcloud compute networks delete tier-vpc --quiet</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Web to app | Allowed on 8080 |
| Web to database | Blocked |
| Service accounts in rules | Harder to misuse than network tags |
| Connectivity Tests | Show the rule that blocks a path |
